Answer: 40.0% (28 out of 70) of non-MPR patients have high Texp cell levels that predict favorable recurrence-free survival despite lack of pathological response.

Method: Among the 70 non-MPR patients in the NSCLC anti-PD-1 cohort, high Texp was defined as the per-patient proportion of Texp (exhausted/expanded) cells within the total Tex (exhausted T cell) compartment exceeding the non-MPR median (Texp.in.Tex.relevant*10 > 8.05, corresponding to ~80.5% Texp among Tex). This threshold was chosen because the continuous Texp variable at this split was a highly significant predictor of recurrence-free survival (log-rank p = 0.0006; Fisher exact p = 0.001). At this threshold, 32 of 64 evaluable non-MPR patients were Texp-high, and 28 of those 32 (87.5%) had no recurrence during follow-up, yielding 28/70 = 40.0% of all non-MPR patients.
